target_game: fantasy RPG with a Three.js/Vite renderer
poly_target: 300–800 triangles — enough surface detail to read well from game camera distance, not so many that it is expensive
material_style: MeshStandardMaterial with roughness 0.75–0.95, low metalness (0.0–0.05) unless the asset is metal or crystal
size_reference: asset should fit inside a 2×2×2 unit bounding box
technique_notes: LOW-POLY STYLE: prefer IcosahedronGeometry(r, 1–3) or custom BufferGeometry — keep faces faceted, avoid over-subdivision
For faceted low-poly look: call geometry.computeVertexNormals() OR leave normals as flat face normals — do NOT smooth if targeting low-poly style
UV coordinates are required — use spherical projection for round shapes, box projection for blocky shapes

Vertex color painting is REQUIRED for organic assets (rock, tree, wood, dirt) — add per-vertex RGB variation using FBM noise evaluated at each vertex 3D position. Pattern: geo.setAttribute('color', new THREE.Float32BufferAttribute(colors, 3)); material.vertexColors = true;
Vertex colors must be computed from the vertex's 3D position (not UV or buffer index) so they are seam-free and survive mergeVertices(). Use a small hash-based noise function seeded by vertex XYZ.
Slight vertex displacement (amplitude 0.05–0.12) adds organic character without increasing face count
Set roughness and metalness explicitly on every material — never leave as default (0.5/0.5)
